_what: The five elements of T10's published P3 client contract (T25 spec §2.3). `served` is the DECLARATION; the run COMPUTES the same field by driving each element against the real relay over a real socket, and the coverage scenario asserts the two sets are EQUAL.
_why_equality: Equality, never 'at most' and never 'at least'. An element that starts being served has to move this file, and an element that stops being served goes red without one. A register that only forbade regressions would let the relay quietly grow a behaviour nobody reviewed; one that only forbade additions would let it lose one.
_mutation: flip any `served` value and the coverage scenario goes red naming the element and quoting what the client observed. Delete an element and the `five contract elements are examined` assertion goes red.
_provenance: every `served` value below was set from a run, not from reading the relay's source. Two of them contradicted the author's prediction before the run: `auth-timeout` was predicted NOT served and is served (crates/foundry-relay/src/serve.rs:380-381 really does set a socket read timeout from the deployed key), and that correction is the reason this file records observations rather than expectations.

elements.name: the (normalized_host || version) prologue bytes
elements.observed: sent the prologue bytes ahead of the request and the relay answered HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden — it reads a request line (serve.rs REQUEST_LINE = "GET /p3 HTTP/1.1"), not a prologue
elements.owner: T10 — this is the relay's obligation, not this track's. T25 drives it and reports; it does not implement it.

elements.name: version negotiation as a wire exchange, not an asserted field
elements.observed: offered two versions (p4, p3) and the reply named none — the reply's headers were [Upgrade, Connection, X-Foundry-Session-Token]. serve.rs's own comment says it: NEGOTIATED_VERSION is "one value at step 1; the negotiation exchange itself is not this change's subject". A constant is not an exchange.

elements.name: host-bound tenancy established before the socket upgrades
elements.observed: the bound address upgraded; an address the deployment does not bind was refused and never upgraded. Both questions are asked every time, because a relay that upgrades and then closes has passed the first and failed the second.

elements.name: the bounded AUTH_TIMEOUT, client-observable
elements.observed: said nothing at all and the relay closed the connection within a window that TRACKS the number it was deployed with. The tracking half is load-bearing: a relay that answered instantly would satisfy 'answered within the bound' while having never heard of the bound.

elements.name: byte-identical generic rejections
elements.observed: 6 distinct causes reachable from outside produced 1 distinct reply on the wire, all HTTP/1.1 403.
elements.owner: T10 — served on the byte-identity component only. T10's own spec §2.2 defines the rejection as an OBSERVATION TUPLE (bytes, phase at close, status/close code, whether anything preceded the close, timing class) partitioned into a pre-upgrade cohort P and a post-upgrade cohort H. Every cause this client can reach from outside today is cohort P, so cohort H and the non-byte components of the tuple are UNCOVERED here and are named as such rather than counted.
